subject: old calendar pages
title: What If 10 Days Vanished From the Calendar? In 1582 They Did

scenes.text: What if ten days vanished from the calendar? In 1582 they did, overnight.
The old Roman calendar ran 11 minutes long every year. By 1582 it had drifted ten days off the seasons.
So Pope Gregory ordered a fix: people went to bed on October 4th and woke up on October 15th.
Protestant countries refused. For decades, crossing a border changed the date.
Britain held out until 1752 and had to drop 11 days. A Hogarth painting shows a banner demanding them back.
Russia waited until 1918 and lost 13 days. Which is why its October Revolution is celebrated in November.

description:
What if ten days vanished from the calendar? In October 1582 they did: the Julian year ran about 11 minutes too long, so by then the calendar had drifted ten days from the seasons. Pope Gregory XIII's fix meant October 4 was followed directly by October 15 in Catholic countries.
Protestant states followed later; Britain dropped 11 days in September 1752, and Russia dropped 13 in February 1918, which is why the October Revolution is marked in November.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Nobody born between October 5 and 14, 1582 had a birthday that year in Rome or Madrid. What date would you delete, and what should we run through next?
